title_en: Ma Xu v. Li Ying and Liang Gan — dispute over compensation for tort damages
keywords_en: civil; tort liability dispute; second instance; Intermediate People's Court; Guangdong Province; natural person; General Principles of the Civil Law; determination of joint tort liability; liability of guardian; reduction of liability due to mixed fault; determination of the scope of compensation; partially upheld; injury caused by setting off fireworks; tort by a minor; compensation for personal injury; principle of fairness; Liang Gan tort compensation dispute
full_text_en:
Ma Xu v. Li Ying and Liang Gan — dispute over compensation for personal injury

Plaintiff: Ma Xu, male, 9 years old, student at Nanshan Central Primary School, Shenzhen, Guangdong Province.

Legal representatives: Ma Haishen and Kang Sujie, employees of Shenzhen Nantou Heliport, father and mother of the plaintiff Ma Xu.

Defendant: Li Ying, female, 9 years old, student at Nanshan Central Primary School, Shenzhen, Guangdong Province.

Legal representatives: Li Shuqing and Zheng Xiuyin, employees of Shenzhen Nantou Heliport, father and mother of the defendant Li Ying.

Agent ad litem: Xu Qingfeng, attorney at Shenzhen Shanren Law Firm.

Defendant: Liang Gan, male, 13 years old, student at Nanshan Central Primary School, Shenzhen, Guangdong Province.

Legal representatives: Liang Jin and Mao Xiuzhen, employees of Shenzhen Nantou Heliport, father and mother of the defendant Liang Gan.

The plaintiff Ma Xu, through his legal representatives Ma Haishen and Kang Sujie, filed a lawsuit with the Nanshan District People's Court of Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, against the defendants Li Ying and Liang Gan regarding a dispute over compensation for personal injury.

The plaintiff's legal representatives alleged: The plaintiff Ma Xu's right eye was injured by fireworks set off by the defendants Li Ying and Liang Gan, resulting in permanent disability. They requested that the defendants be ordered to compensate for medical expenses, transportation costs, lost wages, nutrition fees, future treatment costs, and other expenses incurred as a result of the treatment, totaling RMB 67,300.

The legal representatives of the defendant Li Ying argued: The fireworks were not taken from Li Ying's home but were picked up outside and were not lit by Li Ying; they were later lit by other boys. The injury to Ma Xu caused by the fireworks had no relation to Li Ying, and Li Ying should not be named as a defendant.

The legal representatives of the defendant Liang Gan argued: Although the fireworks that injured the plaintiff Ma Xu were lit by the defendant Liang Gan, the fireworks were provided by Li Ying, the ignition source was provided by Ye Qian, and the plaintiff approached the fireworks to watch after being warned, thereby causing the harmful result. The harmful result was caused by the mixed fault of four persons, and Ye Qian should be added as a co-defendant in this case, with each party assuming corresponding civil liability. Additionally, the plaintiff sought treatment at seven different hospitals before the injury was examined by a forensic medical examiner, which increased the medical expenses; the claim for RMB 60,000 in future treatment costs was unfounded.

The Nanshan District People's Court of Shenzhen, after trial, found the following facts: At approximately 8:00 p.m. on January 29, 1993, the defendant Li Ying was holding a 40-shot "magic bullet" firework and setting it off on the lawn in front of the residential building. The defendant Liang Gan saw this and went to help. Because the magic bullet had no fuse, Liang Gan obtained a small firework from Ye Qian and inserted it into the magic bullet tube. After igniting it, he warned the plaintiff Ma Xu to move away, but Ma Xu did not move away and instead turned his head and looked into the magic bullet tube with his eye. The magic bullet ejected and struck Ma Xu's right eye, and finally the firework exploded in Li Ying's hand. After Ma Xu's right eye was injured, his legal representatives took him to Shenzhen Eye Hospital, Shenzhen People's Court (Note: likely meant Shenzhen People's Hospital), Beijing Tongren Hospital, the First Affiliated Hospital of Shenyang Medical University, the Hospital of the Logistics Department of the Shenyang Military Region, and Fuzhou Lu Jingming Eye Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, among others, for treatment, all without effect. Subsequently, a forensic examination by the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court determined: Ma Xu's right eye suffered from traumatic cataract, with vision only able to perceive hand movements before the eye, constituting a serious injury. Ma Xu spent a total of RMB 2,081 on treatment for the eye injury; transportation and accommodation expenses totaled RMB 2,698.5; and the legal representatives of Ma Xu incurred lost wages and reduced bonuses of RMB 898 due to taking leave to care for Ma Xu's eye injury.

The Nanshan District People's Court held: The defendant Li Ying provided and held the firework while the defendant Liang Gan set it off, causing injury to the plaintiff Ma Xu's right eye. In accordance with Articles 98 and 119 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Li Ying and Liang Gan shall bear civil liability for causing harm to another person's body. Li Ying's conduct was the main cause of the harm and shall bear primary liability; Liang Gan shall bear a certain degree of liability. In view of the fact that the two defendants are joint tortfeasors, in accordance with Article 130 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, they shall also bear joint and several liability. Li Ying and Liang Gan are respectively a person without civil capacity and a person with limited civil capacity. In accordance with Articles 12 and 133 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, their civil liability shall be borne by their guardians. Ma Xu is only 9 years old and has suffered damage to his right eye, which will inevitably cause difficulties in his future life, studies, and work. To compensate for the losses, the defendants, in addition to compensating for medical expenses, transportation costs, accommodation expenses, and lost wages, should also provide appropriate compensation for the plaintiff's future living expenses. The amount of this compensation shall be determined at the court's discretion based on the current average living standard in society and the defendants' ability to perform. Ma Xu, after being warned by Liang Gan and others, still looked into the firework tube, and his conduct was also one of the causes of the harm. In accordance with Article 131 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, the defendants' civil liability may be appropriately reduced. Ma Xu's guardians, without obtaining the consent of the initial hospital or the defendants, took Ma Xu to five different hospitals outside the city for treatment, incurring unnecessary expenses. Therefore, the additional transportation and accommodation expenses incurred as a result shall be borne by themselves. Ye Qian's provision of an ignition source to Liang Gan was not the direct cause of Ma Xu's injury, and this conduct had no necessary causal relationship with the occurrence of the harmful result. Therefore, the request of Liang Gan's legal representatives to add Ye Qian as a defendant in this case is not accepted. Accordingly, the Nanshan District People's Court, on October 22, 1993, ruled as follows:

1. The plaintiff Ma Xu has incurred treatment expenses of RMB 2,081, transportation expenses of RMB 200, his legal representatives' lost wages of RMB 898, Ma Xu's future living allowance of RMB 20,000, and treatment costs of RMB 10,000, totaling RMB 33,179. Of this amount, the legal representatives of the defendant Li Ying, Li Shuqing and Zheng Xiuyin, shall assume RMB 13,272; the legal representatives of the defendant Liang Gan, Liang Jin and Mao Xiuzhen, shall assume RMB 9,945; and the remaining amount shall be borne by the legal representatives of the plaintiff, Ma Haishen and Kang Sujie.

2. Li Shuqing, Zheng Xiuyin, Liang Jin, and Mao Xiuzhen shall bear joint and several liability for the compensation amount determined in item 1.

3. The request of Liang Gan's legal representatives to add Ye Qian as a defendant is dismissed.

After the first-instance judgment was announced, the defendant Li Ying, through her legal representatives, appealed to the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court on the same grounds as the defense in the first instance.

During the second-instance trial, the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court found that the lost wages incurred by the legal representatives of the appellee Ma Xu due to caring for him amounted to RMB 1,287.25.

The Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court held that the facts found in the first-instance judgment were clear and the allocation of liability was proper; the compensation for treatment expenses, transportation costs, and future treatment costs awarded was reasonable and should be affirmed. The amount of lost wages should be confirmed based on the amount found in the second instance. Regarding the future living allowance, referring to the provision of RMB 6,900 for compensation for loss of one eye in the "Interim Provisions on Work-Related Injuries of the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone," the amount may be appropriately increased to RMB 10,000; the first-instance award of RMB 20,000 was excessive. The appellant's argument that Li Ying had no fault and should not bear civil liability lacks factual basis and is not accepted. Accordingly, the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Items (1) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on July 20, 1994, ruled as follows:

1. Items (2) and (3) of the civil judgment (1993) Shen Nan Fa Min Chu Zi No. 55 of the Nanshan District People's Court of Shenzhen are affirmed;

2. Item (1) of the original judgment is modified as follows: The appellee has incurred treatment expenses of RMB 2,081, transportation expenses of RMB 200, future living allowance of RMB 10,000, treatment costs of RMB 10,000, and lost wages of the legal representatives of RMB 1,287.25, totaling RMB 23,568.25. Of this amount, the legal representatives of the appellant Li Ying, Li Shuqing and Zheng Xiuyin, shall assume RMB 10,600; the legal representatives of the original defendant Liang Gan, Liang Jin and Mao Xiuzhen, shall assume RMB 8,068; and the remaining amount shall be borne by the legal representatives of the appellee Ma Xu.
